tagline: Up the narrow canyon and over the top to Woodruff.
intro: Highway 39 heads east out of Ogden and within three miles is in a very narrow canyon beside a fast-moving river. It comes out at Pineview Reservoir and the high valley around Huntsville, follows the Ogden River past campgrounds shaded by old cottonwoods, then turns north up Beaver Creek through aspen forest and climbs to a pass just below 9,148-foot Monte Cristo Peak. The byway ends at the Monte Cristo guard station. The road mapped here keeps on down the eastern side to Woodruff.
The canyon road charged a toll from 1860 until it became a public road in 1882.
season: Autumn, for the aspen forest along Beaver Creek.

moments.title: Ogden Canyon
moments.text: The road winds through a quartzite gorge carved by the Ogden River, and unlike the other canyons off the Wasatch Front, this one is mostly private property.

moments.title: Pineview Reservoir
moments.text: At the head of the canyon the road reaches the dam, finished in 1937 where three forks of the Ogden River meet, and follows the reservoir's southern edge toward Huntsville.

moments.title: Woodruff
moments.text: Settled in 1870 in the Bear River Valley, the town at the bottom of the long eastern descent is a cold spot that averages only 57 frost-free days a year.

practical: The road is open year-round through Huntsville, but the high section near Monte Cristo is closed in winter, usually from December through April. The canyon stretch is narrow with sharp curves and inconvenient for large RVs.
